- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast shows a sharp drop, adjust downward bias by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is overly optimistic, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect bearish momentum.  
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (mean error < -1.5%), apply mean reversion: shift forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting.  
- If forecast is consistently 1–2% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward correction by 0.5–1.5% per day to align with sentiment drift.
